reference_sql:
-- Step 1: one row per order. Step 2: one row per channel.
WITH order_totals AS (
  SELECT order_id, channel, SUM(net_revenue_eur) AS order_eur
  FROM sales
  GROUP BY order_id, channel
)
SELECT channel, COUNT(*) AS n_big_orders
FROM order_totals
WHERE order_eur > 1000
GROUP BY channel
alternatives: WITH big_orders AS (SELECT order_id, channel FROM sales GROUP BY order_id, channel HAVING SUM(net_revenue_eur) > 1000) SELECT channel, COUNT(*) AS n_big_orders FROM big_orders GROUP BY channel

WITH order_totals AS (SELECT order_id, channel, SUM(net_revenue_eur) AS order_eur FROM sales GROUP BY order_id, channel) SELECT channel, COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE order_eur > 1000) AS n_big_orders FROM order_totals GROUP BY channel

other_way.sql: WITH big_orders AS (SELECT order_id, channel FROM sales GROUP BY order_id, channel HAVING SUM(net_revenue_eur) > 1000) SELECT channel, COUNT(*) AS n_big_orders FROM big_orders GROUP BY channel
other_way.tradeoff: HAVING inside the step keeps only the big orders, but then the step no longer shows every order's value to check.

solver.query:
WITH per_order AS (
  SELECT order_id, channel, SUM(net_revenue_eur) AS order_eur
  FROM sales
  GROUP BY order_id, channel
)
SELECT channel, COUNT(CASE WHEN order_eur > 1000 THEN 1 END) AS n_big_orders
FROM per_order
GROUP BY channel
